st.headline: Asian stocks fluctuate as US rate worries temper tech bounce
st.teaser: Confidence was lifted by data centre operator CoreWeave's earning report and Anthropic's filing.
fullText: HONG KONG – Asian stocks diverged on Nov 11 as renewed optimism over the AI trade was offset by forecast-topping US inflation data and the prospect of a bumper interest rate hike in December .

After last week’s rout fuelled by fears that Democrats would ramp up regulation of artificial intelligence , beaten-down tech stocks have bounced this week on bargain buying and a feeling their fears may have been overdone.
Sentiment was also given a boost by earnings from data centre operator CoreWeave, which said sales would come in at US$13 billion ( S$16.66 billion ) to US$13.3 billion in 2026 , beating estimates.

The news soothed worries about the company’s health after suffering heavy selling in October amid speculation that it could struggle to finance its vast debt pile as borrowing costs continued to rise.
That sparked a period of panic over the tech sector as firms rely heavily on debt to fund their eye-watering AI investments.
Also lifting confidence was Anthropic’s filing showing it planned to raise up to US$64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering , valuing it at as much as US$1.4 trillion.
The maker of AI agent Claude had been expected to raise up to US$100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record.
The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom can last.
Its filing also revealed that revenue soared to US$17 billion in the third quarter, up from just US$1.4 billion in 2025 .

And in another sign of the sector’s health, Bloomberg reported that ChatGPT-maker OpenAI had earned US$10 billion in quarterly revenue for the first time in July-September, thanks to demand for its software.
The figure marked an increase of nearly 50% from the previous three months and a near threefold jump year-on-year.
However, chip giant Nvidia was still in focus following the bombshell revelation of an affair between chief executive officer Jensen Huang and a woman reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy.
The firm is now the subject of a Federal Bureau of Investigation probe .
All three main indexes on Wall Street ended in the red on Nov 10 , snapping a two-day rally, and Asia stuttered.
Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei – where most of Asia’s leading AI-linked firms are listed – continued to rise, with Singapore and Jakarta also up.
But there were losses in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Wellington and Manila.
Traders are also now fretting over the possibility of a bigger-than-expected rate hike by the Federal Reserve when it next meets in December.
US consumer prices rose 0.4% on-month in October, a slowdown from September’s 0.6% but more than the 0.3% forecast.
While the reading reflected a significant moderation in energy price increases, food prices shot higher with medical care, household furnishings and several other categories.
Chicago Fed boss Austan Goolsbee told PBS Newshour the reading was “another distressing report, borderline disturbing”.
The report came hours after Fed governor Christopher Waller called for a swift response to inflation, suggesting he could even support a 50-basis-point hike in December.
A second Fed official, Dallas Fed president Lorie Logan, also signalled strong support for swift action to address inflation.
“Market participants continue to navigate the political implications of the Democratic swee p a nd the economics of AI infrastructure,” said Chris Weston at Pepperstone .
He said investors were “forced to reassess assumptions around future revenues, cash flows and funding conditions”.

“Add a hotter-than-expected US (consumer price) print, a heightened focus on Anthropic’s IP O and a major buyers’ strike on Nvidia, and there’s no shortage of catalysts driving market price action,” he added.
Oil prices edged up after sinking again on Nov 10 in the hope of a US-Iran agreement to end their war and reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz.
International benchmark Brent was hovering around US$92 a barrel, after dropping below US$90 for the first time since August. Both contracts are down around 20% since the start of the month.
In company news, Japanese tech investment giant SoftBank tumbled as much as 8% in Tokyo after reporting a more than US$7 billion loss in the fiscal second quarter. AFP

cna.headline: Tampines Mall gets S$24 million revamp with 21 new brands
cna.teaser: The 31-year-old mall will complete its upgrading works in December, adding 21 brands new to the mall, including 15 making their debut in the east.
fullText: Tampines Mall's S$24 million (US$18.7 million) makeover is concluding, with more beauty stores, dining options and upgraded facilities as part of a revamp set to be completed in December 2026.

The 31-year-old CapitaLand-managed shopping centre, which first opened in 1995, will welcome 21 brands new to the mall, including 15 making their debut in eastern Singapore. Ten returning brands have also refreshed their stores.
One of the biggest changes is the mall's growing focus on beauty, with a cluster of 14 retailers that CapitaLand says is the largest in the east.
Shoppers can expect a mix of beauty brand names such as Sephora and Shiseido, alongside newer additions including Judydoll and Rituals.
Some luxury brands that previously operated through store concessions, including Chanel and Dior, now also have standalone boutiques.

There are also more places to eat, with several restaurants and cafes opening their first outlets in the east. These include Italian restaurant Casa Vostra, Hong Kong's Ging Sun Ho King of Bun, known for its pan-fried pork soup buns, and Charlie's Tea, a Guangzhou milk tea brand making its Singapore debut.
Other additions include Thai-Malay restaurant IM QALB by Pun Im, which has introduced a Tampines Mall-exclusive menu, and Guangzhou dessert cafe Ruxu.

For sports enthusiasts, a larger Decathlon is returning to Tampines Mall with an 18,000 sq ft store carrying more than 6,000 products across over 60 sports. Visitors can also try selected equipment before buying, while services include basic bicycle maintenance and racket restringing.
The revamp extends beyond the stores, with upgraded common areas and facilities. The mall's refreshed interiors also incorporate its familiar Tampines tree motif.
Tampines Mall general manager Adrian Lai said the changes are intended to give shoppers more choices while continuing to serve the community.
The eight-storey mall, located next to Tampines MRT and bus interchanges, currently houses more than 160 stores.

listening.title: Singapore's Green Economy Push in Changi
listening.transcript: Singapore is accelerating its transition towards sustainable aviation by expanding its use of eco-friendly fuels. Changi Airport Group announced today that all departing flights will gradually incorporate sustainable aviation fuel over the coming decade. Officials hope this step will maintain the city-state's position as a regional hub while reducing carbon emissions. Industry experts believe the initiative could set a precedent for air travel across Asia.

economistArticle.title: Lessons from a miserable month for hedge funds
paras: For global hedge fund managers, recent weeks have brought a stark dose of reality. As capital flows relentlessly into artificial intelligence giants, fund managers attempting to diversify into conventional equities, commodities, and emerging markets have suffered dismal returns. What was intended as prudent risk management has instead yielded painful underperformance.

The concentration of market gains in a handful of technology behemoths has created an acute dilemma. Quantitative funds relying on historical statistical arbitrage found their predictive models upended by single-track sentiment. Meanwhile, fundamental stock-pickers who strayed from the narrow path of silicon-chip makers saw their portfolios falter as broader economic indicators flashed mixed signals.

This narrow breadth of market participation poses structural challenges for alternative investment firms. Clients pay lavish management fees expecting uncorrelated returns, yet the current landscape penalizes almost every strategy that eschews the dominant narrative. Attempting to hedge against an AI pullback has proven exceedingly costly, as momentum continues to override traditional valuations.

Ultimately, the month's ordeal underscores the peril of fighting strong secular trends in liquidity-starved markets. Fund managers must now reconcile their fiduciary duties with an unforgiving financial reality: in a regime dominated by single-theme euphoria, conventional wisdom can temporarily become a severe liability.
economistArticle.cn:
对于全球对冲基金经理而言，最近几周带来了残酷的现实教训。随着资金源源不断地流向人工智能巨头，试图多元化投资于传统股票、大宗商品和新兴市场的基金经理遭受了惨淡的回报。原本旨在实施审慎风险管理的策略，反而导致了痛苦的业绩落后。

市场收益集中于少数科技巨头，这造成了严峻的困境。依赖历史统计套利的量化基金发现，其预测模型被单向的主导情绪所打破。与此同时，偏离芯片制造领域这一狭窄路径的基本面选股者则发现，随着更广泛的经济指标释放出矛盾信号，其投资组合陷入困顿。

这种狭窄的市场参与度对替代投资机构构成了结构性挑战。客户支付高昂的管理费是希望获得非相关性的回报，但当下的市场环境几乎惩罚了所有避开这一主导叙事的策略。事实证明，试图针对人工智能回调进行套期保值的成本极其高昂，因为动能持续压倒了传统估值。

归根结底，这个月的惨痛经历凸显了在流动性匮乏的市场中违背强劲长期趋势的危险。基金经理现在必须调和其受托责任与残酷的财务现实：在一个由单一主题狂热主导的机制中，传统智慧暂时可能成为沉重的负担。
